# Award changes

[AwardsAn award is a legal document that outlines the wages and conditions of employment for employees that are covered by it within a particular industry or occupation. Other known term: modern award.](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/taxonomy/term/495 "award") are regularly updated by the Fair Work Commission (the Commission).

The Commission is the national workplace relations tribunal and registered organisations regulator.

Learn more about changes to awards.

## On this page:

- [Major award changes](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/about-us/workplace-laws/award-changes#major-award-changes)
- [Annual Wage Review](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/about-us/workplace-laws/award-changes#annual-wage-review)

- [Related information](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/about-us/workplace-laws/award-changes#related-information)

## Major award changes

A major change to an award can include changing entitlements, responsibilities and conditions for employers and employees covered by an award.

Some significant award updates are highlighted on our [Major award changes](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/about-us/workplace-laws/award-changes/major-award-changes "Major award changes") page.

More information about the full list of awards and changes can be found on the Commission’s [Awards](https://www.fwc.gov.au/agreements-awards/awards) page.

## Annual Wage Review

Every year, the Commission reviews the [National Minimum WageA pay rate that applies to employees not covered by an award or registered agreement. Certain award or agreement free employees may have different pay entitlements depending on whether they have a reduced work capacity because of disability, if they're under the age of 21 or if they are an apprentice or trainee.](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/taxonomy/term/404 "National Minimum Wage (NMW)") and minimum rates of pay in modern awards to decide if they should be increased. This is the [Annual Wage ReviewA review made by the Fair Work Commission on the national minimum wage and pay rates in awards. Any changes that are made begin on the first full pay period on or after 1 July.](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/taxonomy/term/476 "Annual Wage Review") (AWR).

The AWR usually happens between March and June. Any changes generally come into effect on 1 July.

For information about the changes to minimum wages, visit our [Annual Wage Review](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/about-us/workplace-laws/annual-wage-review "Annual Wage Review") page.

For more information about the review process, visit the Commission’s [Annual Wage Reviews](https://www.fwc.gov.au/hearings-decisions/major-cases/annual-wage-reviews) page.

## Modern Awards Review

The Commission can be requested to review Modern Awards by the Minister for Employment and Workplace Relations.

The Commission is currently reviewing 4 priority topics as part of the Modern Awards Review 2023-24:

- Arts and Culture Sector
- Job Security
- Work and Care
- Making awards easier to use

For more information, visit the Commission's [Modern Awards Review 2023-24](https://www.fwc.gov.au/hearings-decisions/major-cases/previous-major-cases/modern-awards-review-2023-24) page.

## 4 yearly reviews

Before 2018, the Commission was required to review all modern awards every 4 years. The 4 yearly review commenced on 1 January 2014. This review is now in its final stages.

The 4 yearly reviews have resulted in common changes across many awards and specific changes to individual awards.

For more information about the 4 yearly review process, visit the Commission’s [4 yearly review](https://www.fwc.gov.au/hearings-decisions/major-cases/4-yearly-review-modern-awards) page.

## Keep up to date

We’ll continue to keep you informed about important workplace changes that affect you.

[Subscribe to email updates](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/about-us/contact-us/subscribe-to-email-updates "Subscribe to email updates") to keep updated and to receive alerts from us – it only takes a few moments to sign up.
